def insert_at_end(arr, element):
  arr.append(element)
  return arr

arr = [1, 2, 3]
new_arr = insert_at_end(arr, 4)
print(new_arr) # Output: [1, 2, 3, 4]
"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Insertion at a Specific Index"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Inserting at a specific index requires shifting existing elements to make space for the new element. This operation has a time complexity of O(n) in the worst case, where n is the number of elements to shift."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"python
def insert_at_index(arr, index, element):
  arr.insert(index, element)
  return arr

arr = [1, 2, 3]
new_arr = insert_at_index(arr, 1, 5)
print(new_arr) # Output: [1, 5, 2, 3]
"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Deletion"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deletion involves removing an element from an array. Similar to insertion, deletion can occur at the end or at a specific index."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Deletion at the End"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Removing the last element is straightforward and efficient (O(1) time complexity)."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"python
def delete_at_end(arr):
  if len(arr) > 0:
    arr.pop()
  return arr

arr = [1, 2, 3]
new_arr = delete_at_end(arr)
print(new_arr) # Output: [1, 2]
"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Deletion at a Specific Index"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deleting an element at a specific index requires shifting the subsequent elements to fill the gap. def delete_at_index(arr, index):
  if 0 <= index < len(arr):
    del arr[index]
  return arr

arr = [1, 2, 3]
new_arr = delete_at_index(arr, 1)
print(new_arr) # Output: [1, 3]

Two common search algorithms are linear search and binary search."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Linear Search"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Linear search iterates through each element of the array until the target element is found or the end of the array is reached. It has a time complexity of O(n) in the worst case."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"python
def linear_search(arr, target):
  for i in range(len(arr)):
    if arr[i] == target:
      return i  # Return the index if found
  return -1  # Return -1 if not found

arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
index = linear_search(arr, 3)
print(index) # Output: 2
"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Binary Search"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Binary search is a more efficient search algorithm that works on sorted arrays. It repeatedly divides the search interval in half. It has a time complexity of O(log n)."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"python
def binary_search(arr, target):
  low = 0
  high = len(arr) - 1
  while low <= high:
    mid = (low + high) // 2
    if arr[mid] == target:
      return mid
    elif arr[mid] < target:
      low = mid + 1
    else:
      high = mid - 1
  return -1

arr = [2, 5, 7, 8, 11, 12]
index = binary_search(arr, 13)
print(index) # Output: -1
